passages.note: Mayfield voted Yea on the motion to concur, adopting the enrolled text of HB 1608; 29 of 92 voting were No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: A school shall notify in writing at least one (1) parent of a student, if the student is an unemancipated minor, of a request made by the student to change the student's: (1) name; or (2) pronoun, title, or word to identify the student.
passages.note: Enrolled text requires notification without a parent asking (excludes rung 3) and drops the earlier written-permission requirement (excludes rung 5); the other part (K-3 sexuality instruction) is a related school provision, not an omnibus.
Third-reading Yea on the House version; the exact third-reading text is not in the sources, and her later concurrence vote on the enrolled text governs.

passages.provision_quote: Sec. 3. (a) An employee or a staff member of a school may only use a name, pronoun, title, or other word to identify a student that is inconsistent with the student's sex if: (1) the student, who is an adult or an emancipated minor; or (2) a parent of the student, who is an unemancipated minor; requests in writing the use of a specific name, pronoun, title, or other word to identify the student.
passages.note: Committee-reported text with a parental-permission clause; not shown to be the text she voted on at third reading, and removed from the enrolled act she later voted for.

rows.reasoning: Mayfield voted Yea (63-29) to concur in enrolled HB 1608 (2023), whose operative section says "A school shall notify in writing at least one (1) parent of a student" of a student's request to change name or pronoun. That matches "Require schools to notify parents": it does not wait for parents to ask, and the enrolled text requires no parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns.
